agents.reasoning: Base rates first. NVDA's own 12-month forward returns since 2002: median +40%, P(down) 22%, P(<-40%) 7%; in setups like today (prior year +10-45%, at a 52-week high, n=25) median +29%. That record is survivorship-biased for a $5.7T leader; the top-dog base rate (Arnott/Wu: largest companies trail their sector by ~4%/yr) and a ~7% market return pull the centre to roughly +5-12%. Round-2 corrections from the supervisor, all accepted: (1) my horizon NTM EPS used a window shifted one quarter forward; on the same Q3 FY28-Q2 FY29 window as today's 19.3-19.7x it is ~$16.7 after a 5% haircut (also FY29 growth trimmed to +15% given consensus 2027 capex growth of only ~+22%, src 27); (2) my fair value used 18x while my base scenario used 15x; I now use one multiple, 16x, in both; (3) FCF conversion of 85% is not supported (Q2 FY27 FCF 36-39% of NI, H1 ~70%), now 75%, with ~$1/share true net cash; (4) the 10Y at 5.24-5.28% is verified at Treasury (src 26) but it is the highest since 2007, not 2002; (5) the Fed-odds source was misattributed; the Dec-9 meeting-specific Kalshi contract shows ~70% for a 25bp hike (search-result snapshot; direct fetch 429) and DeFi Rate 72%, so the macro headwind stands; (6) I dropped the 'historical 17-20x floor' argument. On compression: it has been estimate-driven (FY28 EPS +24% in 90 days while the price rose), so it is real but has not hurt holders; I assume 3.5 more turns (to 16x), while a flat year needs ~14.2x on my EPS, a de-rating that likely needs an EPS break. Fair value $255 (P/E $267, FCF $230, mid-cycle $260) is below my round-1 $296. Scenarios: bear $150 (25%), base $267 (50%), bull $342 (25%, lowered from $370 to an 18x multiple). The ladder is a three-lognormal mixture (sigmas 0.25/0.20/0.18) plus a 5% wide tail component: mean ~$263, median ~$262, P(up) ~61%, P(<$166) ~17%. The ladder sits slightly above the blended fair value because the FCF leg is a deliberately rate-harsh cross-check. Research limits: Kalshi returned 429 and Polymarket's December page was the 2025 market, so Fed odds rest on the Kalshi search snapshot and the DeFi Rate aggregator; the Moody's capex note returned 403. Peer forward EV/EBITDA is estimated from trailing figures and peer growth is 3-year CAGR.
